Commentary.Commentary: Now then, the wicket is assisting the pacers and the Kiwis have a strong pace attack. The Lankans on the other hand, would fancy themselves to take a lead as the score is not a big one. Will we see another session dominated by the ball or will the batters come out on top? Stay tuned to find out in some time.

The Islanders won the toss and elected to bowl and their bowlers have justified their skipper's decision. Lakmal ran through the top order in the first session. Taylor and Watling seemed to build a partnership but the former was dismissed in an unfortunate manner. De Grandhomme also did not contribute a lot. The Kiwis were in dire straits at 64 for 6 but a 108-run stand between Tim Southee and BJ Watling with the former scoring a half ton and the latter missing out by just has given some respectability to New Zealand's total.

So 8 balls is all it took to pick the remaining 2 wickets after the Tea break. End of an excellent bowling performance by the visitors, led by their spearhead Lakmal. He leads them off the field and the Lankans will be the happier side at the moment.

OUT! That is it. Kumara gets his second in the over and third in the innings. The short ball does the trick. It is a bumper on middle, Ajaz Patel looks to pull but gets a top edge towards fine leg where Suranga Lakmal takes a comfortable catch. NEW ZEALAND ALL OUT FOR 178.

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Not a lot of batting left now for the Kiwis. They would hope that Watling, along with the remaining two wickets can add some handy runs. Lanka on the other hand, will look to take the remaining wickets as quickly as possible. Will the hosts reach 200? Join us to find out in a while.

It was Tim Southee who came to their rescue. He along with BJ Watling counter-attacked, the former especially. The pacer took on the Lankan bowlers and scored at will. He did have luck on his side but also played some excellent cricketing strokes. Watling on the other hand, was happy to play second fiddle. The two added 108 for the 7th wicket and they looked like they would take the game away from the visitors. However, a brilliant catch by Karunaratne to dismiss Southee and Lakmal's 5th sees the Lankans go back on top in the contest.

What an entertaining session of cricket we witnessed there. Sri Lanka still ahead in the game but not by much I feel. After heading into the post-Lunch session in deep trouble, they slipped further when they lost Taylor and de Grandhomme in quick succession. At that time, it seemed the Kiwis would struggle to get to 100 but that was not to be.

OUT! Now Wagner goes. Lakmal gets a five-fer. What a day he has had. Short outside off, Wagner looks to slash hard but gets a thick outside edge towards second slip where Kusal Mendis takes a good catch. Great display of bowling from Suranga Lakmal. THAT IS TEA ON DAY 1.

OUT! What a catch! Something special was needed to break this stand and Gunathilaka has provided that. Outstanding by him. Dilruwan tosses this up around off, Southee comes down the track and whips it with the turn towards mid-wicket. He must have thought there are runs on offer as soon as he hit it up but Gunathilaka had different ideas. The Lankan opener, times his leap to perfection, stretches his right hand up and plucks the ball out of thin air. That ends the 108-run stand and also an entertaining, important for the Kiwis and a frustrating innings for the Lankans. Can Sri Lanka now bowl New Zealand out for under 200?

Sri Lanka would love more of the same after the break. However, they would like the other bowlers to give more support to Lakmal. New Zealand on the other hand, will hope Taylor and Watling can build some sort of a stand and take the hosts to safer shores. Will we see the Lankans dominate or will New Zealand fight back? Join us in a while to find out.

The Kiwis though started off nicely, they were put into bat and did well to play the first 45 minutes or so out quite comfortably. Post that, it was the Lakmal show. The pacer, then removed the openers in quick succession. The Lankan skipper then decided to give him an extended spell and Lakmal did not disappoint. He picked up another two and has justified his skipper's decision to bowl first.

Sri Lanka's session, Lakmal's session I should say. He has continuously bowled from one end right from the start. His spell accounted for 12 overs on the trot. He has ran through the top order of the Kiwis and has picked all the 4 wickets which have fallen.

Latham tries to drive it through mid on but gets an outside edge. The ball goes low towards second slip where Mendis takes a very good catch. Latham starts walking back but the umpires ask him to wait as they want to check if it has carried. Replays show that it has easily. Two wickets in two overs for Lakmal, he is on fire at the moment. New Zealand in a spot of bother here.

TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the toss and chosen to field. The visitors have two changes - Roshen Silva comes in for Dhananjaya de Silva and Dushmantha Chameera comes in for Kasun Rajitha. New Zealand are unchanged.

The Lankans will head into the game with a lot of confidence after their excellent fightback. The hosts on the other hand, will look to be clinical this time and bag yet another series win. They are favourites heading into the contest. Stay tuned for the toss.
